title: Charles Schwab Opens Bitcoin And Ethereum Transfers As Crypto Rollout Expands
summary: TL;DR: Charles Schwab is expanding its direct Bitcoin and Ethereum services, including phased external wallet transfers. The move brings digital asset ownership further into the company’s conventional brokerage experience. Charles Schwab is moving its cryptocurrency service closer to the features customers expect from a dedicated digital asset platform. The brokerage has been rolling out direct Bitcoin and Ethereum trading to eligible clients, and its latest account documentation explains how approved customers can transfer supported assets to and from external wallets. For Schwab, that is a meaningful step beyond providing market exposure inside an investment account. Buying Crypto Is Only The Beginning Brokerage customers increasingly want to decide whether to hold digital assets with a financial institution or move them to another approved custody arrangement. Schwab’s transfer functionality is being introduced in phases. Users must meet identity verification requirements and may encounter security checks and waiting periods for approved wallet addresses. The platform also continues to distinguish cryptocurrency from conventional insured bank deposits. The value of Bitcoin and Ethereum is not protected by FDIC insurance merely because the assets are held through a Schwab service. As NewsBTC reported when Schwab introduced direct crypto trading, the rollout has been deliberately gradual. Traditional Brokerages Become Serious Rivals Schwab already has millions of brokerage relationships and well-established infrastructure. Adding cryptocurrency ownership makes those relationships increasingly valuable in a market where digital asset exchanges are competing with conventional financial firms. The company has also discussed expanding its supported assets beyond Bitcoin and Ethereum. The wider trend is clear: investors are increasingly being offered cryptocurrency services through the same institutions they use for stocks and other financial products. The competitive question is no longer simply whether traditional brokerages will support cryptocurrency. It is how much of the customer experience they intend to control. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Crypto Giants Feature In $210 Million Political Donations Report As Regulatory Scrutiny Grows
summary: TL;DR: An October 8 Public Citizen report links corporations and individuals benefiting from cancelled federal enforcement actions to approximately $210.5 million in donations and pledges to Trump-aligned political committees. Major cryptocurrency companies feature among the reported contributors. A report examining corporate political donations and changes to federal enforcement has placed several major cryptocurrency businesses under renewed public scrutiny. Consumer advocacy organisation Public Citizen said companies and individuals connected to beneficiaries of cancelled or curtailed enforcement actions had contributed or pledged roughly $210.5 million to Trump-aligned political committees. The research, originally published October 8, includes cryptocurrency firms such as Crypto.com and Gemini. It should not be described as a brand-new October 16 investigation. The Crypto Industry’s Political Spending According to the report, Crypto.com-associated contributions included $35 million to MAGA Inc. and another $2 million to a separate Trump-aligned committee. Public Citizen also examined contributions involving Gemini and the Winklevoss brothers, alongside regulatory matters affecting the exchange. The watchdog argues that the scale of political spending deserves attention, particularly where companies also benefit from changes in how government agencies pursue enforcement. But political contributions are not proof of an illegal arrangement. The report does not establish that the named donors purchased specific regulatory decisions. A Broader Political Debate The cryptocurrency industry has become increasingly involved in Washington, advocating for clearer legislation and a more predictable business environment. NewsBTC has previously reported on substantial cryptocurrency political contributions, part of a larger push to influence rules affecting exchanges, stablecoins and token issuers. Supporters of those efforts argue that previous regulation created unnecessary uncertainty. Critics say large corporate donors may enjoy disproportionate access to policymakers. Public Citizen’s findings add to that debate while leaving the central legal distinction intact: correlation between donations and enforcement outcomes does not establish corruption. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Binance.US Seeks $100 Million Funding Round At $1 Billion Valuation
summary: TL;DR: Binance.US is reportedly seeking up to $100 million from private investors at a proposed valuation of approximately $1 billion. The financing discussions come as the American exchange attempts to rebuild after several difficult years. Binance.US is reportedly pursuing a $100 million fundraising round as it seeks to strengthen its presence in the American cryptocurrency market. Bloomberg reported on October 15 that the exchange was discussing an investment at a valuation of approximately $1 billion. If completed on those terms, it would represent a sharp reduction from the $4.5 billion valuation attached to its 2022 funding round. The discussions have not been announced as a closed transaction, and the proposed figures could change. Rebuilding A Damaged Business Binance.US once competed aggressively for American cryptocurrency traders but faced major regulatory and operational difficulties. The Securities and Exchange Commission’s earlier proceedings complicated the company’s relationships with banks and other commercial partners. As NewsBTC covered at the time, those disputes included an emergency application involving assets connected to the platform. Conditions have since changed, with US regulators adopting a different approach to digital asset businesses. But a friendlier environment alone does not guarantee that customers return. Fresh funding could support compliance, technology development and new products, while giving Binance.US greater flexibility to compete with established exchanges and brokerages. What The Valuation Suggests A proposed $1 billion valuation is not itself a completed market transaction, but it is a reminder of how substantially expectations for cryptocurrency platforms have evolved since 2022. The next challenge for Binance.US will be demonstrating that investment capital can translate into stronger trading activity and sustainable growth. For now, the fundraising discussions show renewed ambition rather than a finished recovery. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Arbitrum Courts European Investors Managing €800 Billion With New Revenue Pitch
summary: TL;DR: Arbitrum representatives have presented the network’s infrastructure and revenue model to European financial institutions managing substantial assets. The meetings should not be confused with confirmed investment commitments to ARB. Arbitrum is increasingly pitching itself as a blockchain infrastructure business rather than simply another cryptocurrency ecosystem. During institutional meetings reported on October 16, representatives discussed the network’s commercial potential with European banks, wealth managers and other professional investors. The participating organisations were said to represent more than €800 billion in assets under management. That figure describes the institutions attending the presentations. It does not represent money invested in Arbitrum or its native token. Explaining The Business Behind The Blockchain The discussions placed particular emphasis on how blockchain infrastructure can earn fees through licensing, network services and support for financial applications. Research presented alongside WisdomTree material explored Arbitrum’s financial performance and the possibility of building sustainable revenue rather than relying on speculative token trading. Institutional projects using Arbitrum technology are one possible route toward such a model. They demonstrate how a financial business might adopt blockchain infrastructure without requiring its customers to trade ARB directly. Arbitrum’s community has also discussed new ways to generate revenue for its DAO treasury. Interest Is Not Adoption The meetings do not confirm that any participating bank has committed to deploy the technology, purchase tokens or establish a product. For Arbitrum, the next task is converting conversations into actual commercial integrations. Banks will demand clear answers about reliability, compliance, privacy and the economics of using blockchain rails. Still, the change in emphasis is notable. Blockchain companies increasingly want to be assessed on the value of the services they provide, not simply the price of their coins. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

The products focus on decentralised finance, artificial intelligence and blockchain data infrastructure. Eligible investors can gain exposure through managed vehicles rather than purchasing every underlying cryptocurrency themselves. The $2,500 entry level is significantly lower than the sums typically associated with institutional private placements, but the offering should not be mistaken for a mass-market retail investment product. Beyond Bitcoin And Ethereum Grayscale’s decentralised finance portfolio includes projects associated with lending, trading and other blockchain-based financial services. Its AI strategy covers networks involved in decentralised computing and related technology. The partnership illustrates how asset managers are packaging more specialised cryptocurrency themes for investors who already understand conventional investment products. Grayscale has separately explored staking-related changes to its Ethereum and Solana investment structures, reflecting its effort to develop products beyond straightforward token-price exposure. The Important Restrictions Participation in the Republic offering is limited to accredited investors under applicable US securities rules. Private investment products may impose selling restrictions, and their holdings can be considerably less liquid than publicly traded ETFs. The lower minimum also does nothing to eliminate the volatility of the cryptocurrencies inside each portfolio. Still, the arrangement provides another example of how traditional asset managers are attempting to make a wider variety of digital assets accessible through familiar investment structures. title: Deutsche Bank Nears Bitcoin Custody Launch As Crypto Push Expands Beyond Europe
summary: TL;DR: Deutsche Bank is preparing to introduce institutional digital asset custody services, initially targeting professional clients in Germany. The planned platform is part of a wider effort to connect cryptocurrencies and tokenized assets to established banking infrastructure. Deutsche Bank is nearing the commercial launch of its institutional cryptocurrency custody business, another sign that major European lenders increasingly regard digital assets as part of mainstream financial services. Comments reported on October 16 indicated that the German banking giant expects to begin serving institutional customers within weeks. Its offering is intended to support assets including Bitcoin and Ethereum, using technology developed with Swiss digital asset infrastructure company Taurus. This is not a new retail cryptocurrency trading app. The initial market consists of businesses and professional investors with demanding custody and compliance requirements. Why Banks Are Entering Custody Holding cryptocurrency for institutional clients involves more than storing private keys. Banks must address asset segregation, operational controls, reporting, insurance arrangements and regulators’ expectations. The service would allow eligible institutions to interact with digital assets through a familiar banking relationship rather than exclusively relying on specialised cryptocurrency companies. Traditional finance is already developing related infrastructure. Projects involving blockchain settlement and tokenized deposits illustrate how established financial businesses are adapting their systems. The Longer-Term Opportunity Deutsche Bank has also discussed tokenized deposits, digital securities and possible expansion into Asian financial centres in 2027. These ambitions remain subject to regulatory approvals and operating arrangements. A planned launch should not be confused with an already operating global service. Nevertheless, the direction is clear. Rather than merely offering clients exposure to cryptocurrency prices, traditional banks increasingly want to provide the infrastructure through which digital assets are held, transferred and managed. title: Binance bStocks Hits $1 Billion As Tokenized Stock Trading Accelerates
summary: TL;DR: Binance says its bStocks tokenized-equity offering has surpassed $1 billion in assets under management, four months after launch. The milestone illustrates growing interest in trading blockchain-based representations of traditional shares. Binance says its bStocks platform has crossed $1 billion in assets under management, marking a significant milestone in its effort to make conventional financial assets tradable through cryptocurrency infrastructure. The company reported the figure on October 15, approximately four months after the product launched. Binance also cited more than $40 billion in cumulative trading volume and an expanded range of tokenized US shares and exchange-traded funds. The numbers suggest that traders are interested in moving between familiar Wall Street exposure and blockchain-based platforms. What Tokenized Stocks Actually Offer Eligible users can trade tokens designed to track exposure to underlying securities held through custody arrangements. Unlike holding ordinary shares directly, these instruments may not confer the same corporate voting or shareholder rights. Their attraction lies in features such as fractional access, transferability and integration with other digital asset products. Binance has already explored using tokenized equity holdings as collateral for derivatives positions, offering investors a reason to hold the instruments beyond simple price exposure. That integration is one potential advantage over conventional brokerages, although it also introduces counterparty, custody and market-structure risks. Regulatory Limits Remain The products are not available to US persons and are subject to eligibility restrictions elsewhere. Tokenization does not remove the obligations surrounding securities trading. For the broader sector, the important question is whether these products can continue attracting demand when crypto market enthusiasm weakens. A $1 billion milestone is meaningful, but sustained growth will depend on transparent backing, dependable liquidity and the ability to offer advantages that conventional market infrastructure cannot easily reproduce. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Bitcoin ETFs Lose $82 Million As BlackRock Leads Friday’s Withdrawals
summary: TL;DR: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $82.4 million in net outflows on October 16. BlackRock’s IBIT accounted for $71.8 million of withdrawals, with Fidelity’s FBTC recording about $10.6 million. BlackRock’s flagship spot Bitcoin ETF accounted for most of the selling as US-listed Bitcoin investment funds closed Friday’s session with net withdrawals of approximately $82.4 million. Farside Investors’ figures show that the iShares Bitcoin Trust, known as IBIT, lost $71.8 million on October 16. Fidelity’s Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund recorded around $10.6 million in net outflows, while the remaining products were broadly flat on the day. That concentration matters because IBIT has become one of the clearest measures of Bitcoin demand through traditional brokerage accounts. Another Uneven Week For ETF Demand The latest withdrawals followed substantial redemptions earlier in the week. October 14 saw roughly $261 million leave the category, followed by a modest return to net inflows on October 15. Friday’s negative session therefore suggests demand remains unsettled rather than following a clear trend. Investors have seen considerably larger individual outflow days in the past. Earlier October withdrawals approached $485 million in a single session, demonstrating how rapidly demand through these products can shift. Context Is Important An ETF outflow is not a complete measure of institutional Bitcoin ownership, and it does not necessarily indicate that every underlying holder has abandoned a long-term position. Net inflows into the US spot Bitcoin ETF market since the products launched remained substantial despite the latest withdrawals. The next trading sessions will be important. A quick recovery would suggest another temporary adjustment, while continued redemptions from IBIT and FBTC would place greater emphasis on whether traditional investors are reducing their exposure amid broader market uncertainty. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Circle Targets 40 New Markets As USDC Push Moves Beyond Crypto Trading
summary: TL;DR: Circle plans to expand USDC infrastructure into approximately 40 developing and emerging markets. The company is targeting international payments and access to digital dollars rather than relying solely on cryptocurrency exchange demand. Circle is looking well beyond cryptocurrency trading as it prepares to extend USDC’s reach into approximately 40 emerging and developing markets. CEO Jeremy Allaire outlined the ambition during discussions surrounding the October 16 international financial meetings in Bangkok. The strategy focuses on places where businesses and individuals want access to dollar-denominated payments but may face expensive or inefficient conventional banking arrangements. The opportunity is straightforward: a stablecoin that can move between compatible wallets at any hour could offer a useful payment alternative. The difficult part is connecting those wallets to actual financial activity. From Exchange Balances To Everyday Payments USDC has long been widely used by cryptocurrency traders as a dollar-linked asset. Circle now wants to make it part of cross-border invoices, business settlement and consumer payments. That requires more than issuing tokens. Businesses need reliable local currency conversion, banking connections, compliance arrangements and confidence that USDC can be redeemed as intended. Circle has increasingly built partnerships around these services. Existing stablecoin initiatives, including creator payouts and digital payment programmes, show how digital dollars can be incorporated into familiar financial experiences. Expansion Will Be Uneven Regulation is likely to determine the pace of Circle’s international push. Some countries welcome stablecoin payment infrastructure, while others restrict foreign currency access or require substantial local licensing. Tether’s USDT is also already entrenched across a number of international markets. Circle must therefore establish the practical value of USDC for customers who may never buy Bitcoin or speculate on another cryptocurrency. If the strategy succeeds, its next stage of growth could depend less on crypto market cycles and more on the ordinary movement of money. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Judge Rejects Gemini And CFTC Bid To Overturn $5 Million Settlement
summary: TL;DR: A federal judge has rejected a joint attempt by Gemini and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to overturn the exchange’s $5 million settlement. The decision leaves the existing judgment in place despite the regulator’s changed approach to cryptocurrency enforcement. Gemini has failed in an unusual attempt to undo a regulatory settlement, despite having the very agency that brought the original case on its side. US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein rejected a joint motion by the exchange and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission seeking to vacate a consent judgment entered in January 2025. The settlement arose from allegations that Gemini misled the regulator during its review of a proposed Bitcoin futures product in 2017. Gemini agreed to pay a $5 million penalty and accepted a permanent injunction. When Regulators Change Their Minds The CFTC subsequently reconsidered the original enforcement case as its digital asset priorities evolved. Together with Gemini, it asked the court to revisit the settlement. That is a very different situation from the more familiar legal battle in which an exchange disputes a regulator’s allegations. This time, both parties wanted relief from the court’s earlier judgment. But a change in enforcement policy does not automatically erase a final court order. The judge found that the arguments presented did not satisfy the legal standards for reopening the settlement. The decision is significant for other cryptocurrency businesses hoping that a more accommodating federal regulatory environment might undo historical enforcement outcomes. What Changes For Gemini? In the immediate term, very little. The settlement remains in effect and the court has not imposed a new fine. The wider message is more important: courts retain control of their judgments, even when a regulatory agency changes its view of a case. Washington’s approach to cryptocurrency may have become more favourable, but companies cannot assume that previously approved settlements will disappear alongside the political circumstances in which they were reached. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.
